name: ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2027

qualifier.rule: Q1 (Qualifier winner) goes straight into the group stage; Q2-Q4 play the Super Series and its winner (SSW) joins the group stage.
qualifier.assignment: TBC: which of Q1 and SSW is Qualifier A. Until confirmed, each simulation draws it 50/50.

sources: ICC media release 'ICC revamp formats for marquee men's events' (15 Jul 2026)
ICC media release 'ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2027 schedule revealed' (1 Oct 2026)
Wikipedia: 2027 Cricket World Cup (revision 1379170381): 57 fixtures, venues, scorecard ids
Wikipedia: 2027 Cricket World Cup qualification (direct qualifiers by ODI ranking on 30 Sep 2026)
assumptions: TBC Qualifier A/B: whether the Qualifier winner or the Super Series winner joins Group A is not published; simulated 50/50.
TBC Super Series: 3 round-robin matches (ICC and Wikipedia); one report says two matches. Order of the 3 TBA fixtures is assumed Q2 v Q3, Q3 v Q4, Q2 v Q4 (order doesn't change the outcome).
TBC Best 4th-placed team: compared on points, then wins, then NRR (groups are the same size, so points compare fairly). Equal points and wins are split by a random draw.
TBC Super 7: no points carried over from the group stage (21 matches = every pair plays once; the release mentions no carry-over).
TBC Knockouts: a washed-out semi-final sends the higher-placed Super 7 team through; a washed-out final is shared; ties go to a super over (simulated 50/50). As in 2019 and 2023.
Home advantage applies only to a team playing in its own country: South Africa in South Africa, Zimbabwe in Zimbabwe, Namibia in Windhoek (if it qualifies). Same rule as every other match.
NRR is not simulated: equal points and wins are split by a random draw.
